A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OneCAT, with matching authors, architecture and principal experiments. All 22 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v3 were readable, including figures and equations. V1 ends with references; v3 adds Appendices A–E.

before.justification: V1 reports original OneCAT understanding, generation and editing results, qualitative outputs, and inference measurements in Tables 3–9.

after.justification: V3 retains those original benchmark results and adds distillation, teacher, token-ratio, adapter and scaling experiments, including analyses in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: Section 4.1.2 changes the reported distillation-loss weight from 0.2 to 0.02. The three-expert architecture, scale-aware adapter, attention mechanisms and staged training otherwise remain intact. Expanded descriptions of adapter placement, scale schedules and guidance do not establish additional algorithm changes.

E1.justification: The main evaluation benchmarks and tasks are retained. Section 5 revises the additional 3M Stage-3 examples from in-house synthetic instructions to public sources covering VQA, art, counting and documents. New ablations use LLaVA-665K instruction data. The expanded Stage-2 source list primarily supplies provenance rather than establishing that every listed dataset was newly introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 3–4 add VoRA and SAIL to understanding comparisons. More substantially, v3 introduces controlled comparisons against EvE and VoRA distillation strategies in Table 9, an alternative Qwen2.5-VL teacher in Table 10, and encoder-based late fusion in Table 14. These extend comparison beyond v1's end-to-end benchmark and latency evaluations.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce controlled training protocols: 8B-token distillation followed by LLaVA-665K fine-tuning, fixed text/understanding budgets with varying generation budgets, and fusion comparisons using a randomly initialized vision encoder. Section 4.3 also revises the stated maximum generated-image side from 1728 to 1776 pixels, although Table 1 retains 1728. These reported changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V1 lacks component ablations. V3 Section 7.5 tests distillation targets, teacher choice, task-token ratios and SAA removal. Appendix C adds fusion, distilled-token and training-scale analyses; Appendix D adds feature-map and Fourier analyses examining the scale-dependent information motivating SAA.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. V3's new tables and curves retain point-estimate reporting; averages across benchmarks are not repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: OneCAT's headline scores in Tables 3–7 are unchanged, but v3 adds substantial ablation and scaling results. New controlled tests report average scores of 31.4 without distillation versus 35.3 with all-layer distillation, and GenEval 81.2 with SAA versus 78.1 without; these are not version-to-version gains. Comparator results and qualitative outputs are added. The 1024×1024 TTFT comparison, 0.216 versus 0.092 seconds, is removed, and Figure 7's final editing case changes its prompt and outputs.

T1.justification: New Appendix A formally specifies recursive multiscale quantization, binary spherical quantization, autoregressive factorization, and the within-scale conditional-independence assumption. Appendix B supplies explicit guidance equations. This adds mathematical definitions and assumptions absent from v1, largely as background and implementation formalization, without new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V3 foregrounds customized-teacher distillation as a contribution addressing small-teacher supervisory bottlenecks. Its abstract removes the open-source qualifier from the superiority claim, and its introduction broadens state-of-the-art wording beyond pure decoder-only unified models. The central claims about unified understanding, generation, editing and efficient autoregressive inference remain.

C2.justification: V3 adds substantive interpretations connecting teacher instability to parameter misalignment, explaining the benefits of all-layer and joint visual/text distillation, and motivating the generation-token allocation through limited interference with understanding. Appendix C also reports early and late fusion as comparable in accuracy under its controls, qualifying the architectural advantage as computational efficiency. These interpretations were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B disclose exact aspect-ratio scale schedules and guidance equations and strengths: 20 for text-to-image, and image/text strengths of 1/3 for editing. V3 also identifies Qwen2-VL recaptioning, JourneyDB prompt provenance, detailed training-data sources and ablation recipes. These substantially expand reproducibility information without establishing a change in code availability.

R1.justification: V3 adds relevant work including VoRA, SAIL, Synergen-VL, native-multimodal scaling research and reconstruction alignment, alongside numerous data-source citations. It introduces a specific critique of small-ViT distillation teachers. The existing four-part related-work organization and overall positioning around encoder-free unified autoregression remain.

P1.justification: V3 extensively rewrites the introduction and method/training exposition, organizes the introduction around architecture and training, consolidates the architecture discussion under Modality-MoE, and shortens the efficiency narrative. Qualitative evaluation receives a separate subsection, and structured appendices provide background and implementation explanations. This exceeds simple additions or renumbering.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn, Table 2 is restructured, Figures 6–7 revise prompt/panel displays, and the two efficiency tables are merged. New ablation tables, learning curves, fusion diagrams, frequency visualizations and qualitative panels substantially expand presentation. Some Appendix E editing examples redisplay images already present in Figure 2 rather than constituting new results.

improvement.justification: V1 claims benefits from distillation and SAA without component-level validation. V3's Section 7.5 and Appendices C–D substantially address that deficiency through controlled ablations, scaling studies and feature analyses; explicit schedules, guidance settings and data provenance also improve reproducibility. These gains outweigh the limited losses and inconsistencies, despite unchanged headline scores. Missing uncertainty estimates, broader superiority wording and the conflicting 1728/1776-pixel settings remain weaknesses.
